exercises.heading: Section 13.4 Exercises
exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, select the most representative decibel level for each sound.

problem.paragraph: Gas lawn mower: 70 dB, 100 dB, 120 dB
Radio playing loud enough to sing along to at home: 20 dB, 50 dB, 70 dB
Office noise on a floor of people working at desks: 40 dB, 60, dB, 80 dB
Conversation in a quiet room: 60 dB, 80 dB, 100 dB
Fast-moving train passing by when sitting in a car about 20 ft from the tracks with windows down: 40 dB, 60 dB, 80 dB

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, state the requested note.

problem.paragraph: What is one half-step above G#?
What is one whole step down from G♭?
What is three half-steps above D?
What is two whole steps down from A#?
What is two half-steps down from E?
What is an octave above B4?
What is two octaves below F5?
What is three octaves above G2?
What is an octave below G2?
Given that the frequency of $$A_{4} = 440{Hz}$$ , what is the frequency of A1?
Given that the approximate frequency of $$F_{4} = 349{Hz}$$ , what is the approximate frequency of F5, rounded to the nearest whole number?
Given that the approximate frequency of $${A_{4}}^{\#} = 233{Hz}$$ , what is the approximate frequency of A6#, rounded to the nearest whole number?
Given that the approximate frequency of $$D_{4} = 294{Hz}$$ , what is the approximate frequency of D2, rounded to the nearest whole number?
Given that the approximate frequency of $${G_{4}}^{\#} = 349{Hz}$$ , what is the approximate frequency of G3#, rounded to the nearest whole number?
